---
title: 'Machine Storage Health'
description: 'Measure, triage and safely reclaim disk space on Macs, Linux devboxes and self-hosted runners with ttr storage.'
updatedAt: '2026-10-23'
---

Every Tuturuuu machine (the M4 Mac, Linux devboxes and VMs, self-hosted CI
runners) uses one tool for storage triage: `ttr storage`. It reports headroom,
ranks consumers by the bytes deleting them would actually free, suggests exact
cleanup commands, and applies only safe, bounded cleanup on request.

## Daily triage

```bash
ttr storage status             # free/used/pressure and inodes per volume (exit 2 when critical)
ttr storage analyze            # ranked consumers by category (add --json)
ttr storage suggest            # actions: reclaimable bytes, risk, exact command
ttr storage prune              # dry run of the default safe categories
ttr storage prune --apply      # re-verifies every fence, then applies the plan
ttr storage fleet              # disk headroom reported by every devbox runner
```

`analyze` and `suggest` walk large trees (Bun cache, stale `node_modules`,
every worktree) and take a few minutes on a busy Mac; run them through
`ttr resources run --` when other lanes are validating. `suggest` caches its
top actions in `~/.tuturuuu/storage/last-suggest.json`.

## Measure real bytes, not apparent bytes

| Platform | Method | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (APFS) | `getattrlist` `ATTR_CMNEXT_PRIVATESIZE` per file, through the system Python | Bun's `node_modules` are APFS clones of `~/.bun/install/cache`; `du` counts shared blocks once per clone. |
| Linux | Allocated blocks (`st_blocks`), hard links counted once per run | Bun's Linux backend hard-links from its cache. |

Never use `du -L`: it follows Bun's workspace symlinks and reported 300 GiB for
`apps/web` alone. A fresh worktree costs about 0.3 GiB unique (source only)
and about 250k inodes, not the 4–9 GiB `du` shows. `bun worktree:footprint`
reports the per-worktree breakdown.

## Thresholds

| Pressure | Rule (any one) |
| --- | --- |
| `critical` | free < `TTR_STORAGE_MIN_FREE` (15 GiB), free < `TTR_STORAGE_MIN_FREE_PERCENT` (5%), or free inodes < `TTR_STORAGE_MIN_FREE_INODE_PERCENT` (5%) |
| `low` | within twice any threshold |
| `ok` | otherwise |

Free space is what an unprivileged user can allocate (`statfs` `bavail`). On
APFS every volume shares its container's free space and inode tables grow on
demand, so the inode percentage only matters on ext4/xfs. Invalid threshold
values fall back to the default with a warning.

## Disk-aware admission

`ttr resources` checks the volume holding a heavy command's working directory
before queueing it. At `critical` it refuses with exit code 75 and prints the
top non-high actions from the last `ttr storage suggest`; at `low` it warns and
continues. A failed probe is UNKNOWN and is refused too, with the probe error
and the override. Once queued, the lane queue re-checks free disk at dequeue
(`TTR_STORAGE_MIN_FREE`, `TTR_STORAGE_MIN_FREE_PERCENT`, and
`TTR_STORAGE_MIN_FREE_INODE_PERCENT`) and holds the job,
failing closed, until headroom returns.

- `--ignore-disk` (or `TTR_RESOURCES_IGNORE_DISK=1`) overrides both checks
  once. Prefer reclaiming space.
- `--hosts` dispatch skips the queue-time refusal; it applies its own local
  disk gate per placement, including inode pressure. Both placement and dequeue
  probe the command directory selected by `--cwd`, `--dir` or `-C`.
- With `--offload auto`, a critical local disk counts as saturated, so the
  exact pushed commit runs on a devbox runner when one is eligible.
- Commands nested inside an admitted job are not checked again.

## Fleet headroom

Each devbox agent adds a bucketed disk report to its existing heartbeat:
`resources.disk = { freeGiB, freePct, inodeFreePct? }`. Values are
conservative lower bounds (GiB steps 0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 50, …;
percentages in 5% steps), about 35 bytes against the 4 KiB heartbeat cap. The
probed path is the agent's working directory, or
`TUTURUUU_DEVBOX_STORAGE_PATH`. The web route (zod `.strict()`) and the
devbox-control Worker (`typeof` checks, no coercion) both reject malformed
reports.

```bash
ttr storage fleet          # every registered runner, critical hosts first (exit 2 if any)
ttr resources offload      # blockedBy=low_disk when every trusted runner is critical
```

Offload selection skips a trusted runner that reports critical disk. Runners
that do not report disk yet (older agents) stay eligible and show as
`unreported`. No new timer or controller is involved: the heartbeat is the
transport.

## Categories

| Category | What | Risk | `prune` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `worktrees` | Linked worktrees, classified `dirty`, `unmerged`, `merged-clean`, `orphaned`, with owner and hold status | safe for merged-clean | named only |
| `node-modules-stale` | Bun stores with far more `.bun` entries than `bun.lock` packages (diverged private clones) | moderate | named, one `--path` |
| `build-artifacts` | `.turbo`, `.next`, `.open-next`, `dist`, `build`, `.dart_tool` in checkouts | safe | default, via `bun worktree:prune-artifacts` |
| `rust-target` | `apps/backend/target` | safe | default, via `bun rust-cache prune` |
| `bun-cache`, `npm-cache`, `pub-cache` | Package manager caches. The npm cache root is resolved once (`npm_config_cache`, then `npm config get cache`, then `~/.npm`); `prune` measures that root's `_cacache` and runs `npm cache clean --force --cache <root>` only on a directory owned by you | moderate / safe | named only |
| `xcode-derived-data` | DerivedData project folders idle past `--older-than` | safe | default |
| `xcode-simulators` | Simulators for uninstalled runtimes, each deleted by its own UDID (`xcrun simctl delete <udid>`, never `delete unavailable`) | safe | default |
| `homebrew-cache` | `brew cleanup --prune=<days>` (also removes old formula versions) | safe | named only |
| `docker` | Build cache older than the age bound; unused images. Verified local daemon only | safe / moderate | named only |
| `supabase-volumes` | Supabase CLI local volumes | high | only `--name <volume>`, never attached |
| `tmp-old` | Identified tool scratch dirs (mktemp, `tmp-*`, Vitest, Turbo, Bun, `ttr-*` and similar) directly under a tmp root, idle past the age bound, at least 25 MiB, with no git checkout, linked worktree or bare repository inside | moderate | named only |
| `xcode-device-support`, `gradle`, `playwright` | Rebuildable but costly | moderate | manual command only |
| `trash`, `xcode-archives`, `android-sdk` AVDs, `vm-disks` | User data, signed builds, emulator state, VM images | high | never |

Defaults: `--older-than 7` days, `--max-remove 20G` total per run.

## What is never removed automatically

- Dirty, unmerged, locked, busy (a process `cwd` inside) or current worktrees,
  and the primary checkout.
- Worktrees active in the last 24 hours.
- Any path covered by a hold file. Hold files are `*.txt` in
  `~/.t3/cleanup/holds.d` (or `--holds-dir`, `TTR_STORAGE_HOLDS_DIRS`); one
  absolute path or glob per line, `#` comments. `--holds-dir` and
  `TTR_STORAGE_HOLDS_DIRS` add directories; the shared default is always
  read. A hold covers its path,
  everything below it and everything above it. An unreadable holds directory,
  or any non-comment line that is not an absolute path or glob, stops the run
  with the file and line; fix or comment out the line.
- Any path a process may be using. Right before each removal, every process's
  working directory (`lsof -d cwd`, checked against the full `ps` table) and
  every open file under the path (`lsof +D`) are re-checked. A failed scan,
  any `lsof` diagnostic, or an uninspectable live process of this user means
  use is not proven absent, and the step is skipped. Uninspectable processes
  of other users (including root) are tolerated only under the private-tree
  rule below. `ps` and `lsof` run by absolute path and scripts by the
  absolute runtime, so a shim directory on `PATH` cannot answer for them.
- Worktrees whose ignored files are not rebuildable. `git worktree remove`
  deletes ignored files without `--force`, so a worktree is kept when
  `git ls-files -o -i --exclude-standard --directory` lists anything outside
  build artifacts, `node_modules` and `target` (for example `.env.local` or
  `tmp/agent-coordination/`); the dry run names those paths.
- Trees with entries this user does not own, or with a group- or
  world-writable directory (`mode & 0o022`), checked in the pre-scan and
  again before every unlink. Running as root removes only fully root-owned
  trees.
- Anything reached through a symlink or across a mount. Trees are removed by
  directory identity (device and inode) captured before the checks and
  re-verified before every unlink; a swapped ancestor or a nested mount stops
  the removal, and entries created after the pre-scan are left in place.
- Docker on a remote or unknown engine. Docker steps run only when
  `DOCKER_HOST` is unset and the current context's endpoint is an existing
  local unix socket; the command is pinned to that socket with `-H`.
- `preserve/*` branches and every other ref. Merged-clean worktrees are removed
  with plain `git worktree remove` (no `--force`) and their branch with
  `git branch -d`; git keeps a squash-merged branch, which is reported for a
  human to delete after checking.
- Source, Trash, VM disk images, Xcode archives, AVDs and Supabase volumes not
  named explicitly.

"Merged" means the exact local `HEAD` reached the base: either it is an
ancestor of `origin/main`, or a merged pull request's head is that `HEAD`
(squash merges). An open PR, a closed-unmerged PR or local commits after the
merged head keep the worktree. Every apply step re-reads holds, process
working directories, open files and worktree state immediately before acting.
Idle ages use the newest modification or change time anywhere in a tree (a
deep, recently written file keeps the whole tree); trees over 500,000 entries
or unreadable ones count as recent.

## Process visibility on macOS: private-tree evidence

Decision (orchestrator, 2026-10-23): a non-root user's `lsof` cannot inspect
other users' or root's processes, so strict visibility would skip every
removal on macOS. Removal (manual `prune` and automatic reclaim alike) may
proceed with `private-tree` evidence only when all of these hold:

1. Every live process of the effective user was inspected; only processes of
   other uids may be hidden.
2. The item has a private-tree proof: some directory at or above the rule
   root is owned by the effective user, has `mode & 0o077 == 0` and no ACL;
   every directory from there down to the item is owned by the effective user
   and not group- or other-writable; all on one device.
3. The open-file scan is scoped to the effective user (`lsof -a -u <euid>`).
4. Never when running as root, and only on macOS. Linux stays fail-closed
   until a container-mount check exists.

Receipts and step checks record the evidence level (`private-tree` or
`full-visibility`). Root's processes remain uninspectable under this rule;
that residual is accepted only for proven-private trees. Idle Xcode
DerivedData usually qualifies through `~/Library/Developer` (0700, no ACL).
Worktrees and their artifacts under `~/.t3` do not qualify unless that tree
is 0700; ttr never changes permissions to make something qualify.

Regression coverage: `packages/sdk/src/cli/storage-privacy.test.ts` (scan
rules per platform and uid, the proof's failure modes, scoped `lsof`, manual
prune wiring) and `storage-liveness.test.ts` (strict scan parsing).

## Stale `node_modules`

`bun install` never removes old `node_modules/.bun/<pkg@version>` entries. On
APFS the old entries become private copies once the cache is refreshed; the
main checkout held about 10 GiB this way. The fix is a reinstall, queued
through `ttr resources`:

```bash
ttr storage prune --category node-modules-stale --path <checkout>        # dry run
ttr storage prune --category node-modules-stale --path <checkout> --apply
```

This removes `node_modules` and runs `ttr resources run -- bun install
--frozen-lockfile`. It refuses while another process works inside the
checkout. A shared primary checkout needs its owner's approval first.

## Per-OS commands

### macOS (APFS)

```bash
diskutil apfs list | grep -E 'Capacity (In Use|Not Allocated)'
df -h /System/Volumes/Data      # the Data volume holds user files
xcrun simctl list devices booted
xcrun simctl shutdown all       # a booted simulator mounts ~220 GB of phantom DeviceFS size
tmutil listlocalsnapshots /     # local snapshots pin deleted blocks
```

### Linux devbox or runner

```bash
df -h / /var/lib/docker
df -i /                         # inodes; ext4 tables are fixed at mkfs
docker system df
journalctl --disk-usage
```
Self-hosted runner jobs remove their own `start-source-<run>-*` checkout in an
`if: always()` step; sweep leftovers only from completed runs.

## Ownership

Run `ttr storage prune --apply` only on a machine you own. Devbox VMs and CI
runner hosts belong to their host owner; report suggestions to that owner
instead. On the M4 Mac the Mastermind daily cleanup task uses the same hold
files and busy/PR-state rules, so a hold written for one tool protects the path
from both.
